profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
Trends in technology are important to me, but they move incredibly quickly.  In 2005, the software stack was much more limited and required much more effort to do basic tasks.  Today, so many options exist in the software stack and more options are being added constantly.  As a software developer and engineer, I see it as my personal responsibility to keep up to date with the latest technology trends and stacks.  This is why you will find me working with things like JavaScript, React.js and Redux today.  Tomorrow though, you'll find me experimenting with various new ideas to add to my personal stack.

These are my most valued qualities: cutting edge, always learning, pragmatic, thoughtful, intuitive.  Done is better than perfect.  If there is a problem to be solved, I will focus and apply what I know to solve it.  All other times, I keep constant vigilance on the technology trends so I can modify my own workflow to remain as productive as possible.  I believe in clean, organized and easily maintainable code and designs

projects.title: Windward Tutor
projects.description:
Worked with a range of tools for the web such as ASP.NET MVC, Entity Framework, HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery JSON, C# and SQL Server to create a website designed to teach clients how to use our software.

This project started with a blank editor and an idea which I have brought forth during breaks from school to be the website it is today, with plenty of improvements planned for the future.

projects.title: SureBot Ohms (ECE202)
projects.description: This was a sophomore design project.  The only restrictions were that we had to use knowledge learned in one of the first two circuit theory courses.  We chose to make a game with the objective of teaching new students binary/decimal conversion and boolean algebra, and we used an Arduino combined with an LCD screen and keypad to accomplish the task.  The majority of the project was in writing C code to work on the Arduino, with a large amount of troubleshooting and debugging.
